content: Etravirine reduces the plasma levels or effects of ixabepilone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Ketoconazole, being a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate, may elevate etravirine plasma concentrations. Conversely, etravirine may reduce ketoconazole plasma levels. Dose adjustments of ketoconazole should be considered based on co-administered drugs. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of lansoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Lapatinib increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of lapatinib through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Leflunomide increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may elevate CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. No quantitative data is available on the effects of CYP3A4 inducers on amlodipine. Blood pressure should be closely monitored when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. Levoketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Levoketoconazole, being a CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate, may elevate etravirine plasma concentrations. Conversely, etravirine may reduce levoketoconazole plasma levels. Dose adjustments of levoketoconazole should be considered based on co-administered drugs. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels of levonorgestrel (both intrauterine and oral forms) by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Alternative or backup contraceptive methods should be used when enzyme inducers are co-administered with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs). Backup contraception should continue for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of linagliptin by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of lomitapide by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of lopinavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, lopinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of loratadine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine increases the plasma levels or effects of losartan by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of losartan by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor interacts with etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. In vitro studies suggest that lumacaftor may induce, while ivacaftor may inhibit, CYP2C9 substrates. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels of lurasidone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. It may be necessary to increase the lurasidone dose after chronic treatment (i.e., seven days or more) with moderate CYP3A inducers. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of maraviroc by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Marijuana increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine increases the plasma levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor mavorixafor if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors, and reduce the mavorixafor dose if needed. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; alternative methods should be used if available. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of mefloquine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of mestranol by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of methadone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Methylprednisolone decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of methylprednisolone through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Metronidazole increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Miconazole vaginal increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of midazolam by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of mifepristone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Mifepristone increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine through the same mechanism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended by the manufacturer. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of mirtazapine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Mitotane decreases the plasma levels of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. Monitor when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates for possible dosage adjustments. Modafinil increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of modafinil by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of naldemedine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Simulation using physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling suggests that moderate CYP3A4 inducers decrease naldemedine exposure. Etravirine increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Etravirine increases the plasma levels or effects of nateglinide by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, nateglinide increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nefazodone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Nelfinavir increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nelfinavir through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Nevirapine decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nicardipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Nifedipine increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nifedipine through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Nilotinib increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nilotinib through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine increases the plasma levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If nintedanib adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of nisoldipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Nitisinone increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Nitisinone inhibits CYP2C9. Caution is advised if CYP2C9 substrates are co-administered, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of norethindrone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of norgestrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Moderate CYP3A4 inducers may decrease progestin concentration; consider using additional barrier methods. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of oliceridine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. If co-administration with a CYP3A4 inducer is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, consider reducing the oliceridine dosage and monitor for signs of respiratory depression. Etravirine increases the plasma levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Orlistat decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased HIV viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of osilodrostat by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dose of osilodrostat if necessary based on signs and symptoms during co-administration or discontinuation with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels of ospemifene by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Oxcarbazepine increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, oxcarbazepine decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels of oxycodone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of palbociclib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Parecoxib increases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, etravirine increases the plasma levels or effects of parecoxib by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of pazopanib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases the plasma levels of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. When patients are administered peginterferon alpha-2b with CYP2C9 substrates, the therapeutic effect of these drugs may be altered. Etravirine increases the plasma levels of pentamidine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. There is potential for increased toxicity. Pentobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of pimavanserin by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy. An increase in pimavanserin dosage may be needed. Etravirine decreases the plasma levels or effects of pitolisant by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Pitolisant exposure is decreased by 50% if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers.
